sources.title: Visa Categories
sources.publisher: Directorate General of Immigration & Passports, Ministry of Interior, Government of Pakistan
sources.officialityEvidence: DGIP's live Ministry of Interior page carries a 2026 Government of Pakistan copyright. Its visitor schedules say India and Somalia are List B, Armenia/Israel/Taiwan are in no list, and Afghanistan has a separate policy; the category page was last modified 11 March 2024.
sources.supportingExcerpt: There are 2 countries in list B (i-e. India & Somalia).

sources.title: Visa for Indian Nationals
sources.publisher: Directorate General of Immigration & Passports, Ministry of Interior, Government of Pakistan
sources.officialityEvidence: DGIP's live Ministry of Interior Indian-national page directly states the ordinary Indian visitor obligation and identifies High Commission issuance before travel. It was last modified 4 October 2023 and remains live under the 2026 DGIP site copyright.
sources.supportingExcerpt: A non-extendable tourist visa valid for 14 days is issued by Pakistan High Commission, New Delhi through approved tour operators/travel agents.

sources.title: Visa Policy for Afghanistan
sources.publisher: Directorate General of Immigration & Passports, Ministry of Interior, Government of Pakistan
sources.officialityEvidence: DGIP's live separate Afghanistan policy is on the Ministry of Interior site. It makes visit issuance conditional on a sponsor/guarantor and security consultation, and its Afghanistan-mission route is discretionary; it was last modified 4 October 2023.
sources.supportingExcerpt: All Pakistan Missions abroad, excluding Afghanistan, may grant entry visit visa for 45-days

policies.title: Indian ordinary passports: Pakistan advance tourist visa
policies.summary: Pakistan's live DGIP Indian-national page requires a valid visa and says the short tourist visa is issued by the Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi before travel.
conditions: Applies to an ordinary Indian passport holder undertaking a short tourist visit; the published tourist visa is non-extendable and valid for 14 days.
The tourist visa is issued in advance by the Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi through approved tour operators or travel agents.

The page requires a valid passport and application; visitor, business, transit, Indian-origin, residence, work, religious-tourism, diplomatic/official documents, border-route, police-reporting, security and final-admission arrangements are outside this baseline.

conflicts.explanation: DGIP's separate Afghan policy uses sponsor- and security-conditioned mission visit visas, including a discretionary Afghanistan-mission route. It does not establish a nationality-wide eVisa or one unconditional ordinary visitor baseline.

unresolved.reason: DGIP's tourist schedules do not separately map an HKSAR ordinary passport. Hong Kong appears only in the business-friendly list, which requires business documents, so it cannot establish a short tourist route; PRC or HKSAR-document treatment is not transferred.

DGIP says Israel is not part of any current visitor list. No current Pakistani or Israeli authority directly establishes ordinary Israeli-passport short-visitor eligibility, recognition treatment, issuance timing or an operational route.

DGIP's tourist schedules do not separately map a Macao SAR ordinary passport. No current Pakistani or Macao passport authority establishes a national-passport visitor route; PRC-passport treatment and travel-alert material are not transferred.

DGIP expressly says Taiwan is not part of any list. No current Pakistani or Taiwanese authority directly establishes recognition, ordinary-passport visitor eligibility, issuance timing or an operational route; a Taiwan eVisa page for travel to Taiwan is irrelevant.

Armenia is expressly outside DGIP's current visitor lists. No current Pakistani or Armenian authority directly maps an ordinary Armenian passport to a short-visitor issuance route; online-visa availability and an unnamed 120-country VPA statement are insufficient.

DGIP labels Somalia List B but supplies no List-B tourist eligibility, issuance channel or timing. Somalia's absence from its named eVisa, VPA and List-A schedules is not used as a complement or to disprove an eVisa route.

DGIP's separate Afghan visitor rules require a Pakistan guarantor or sponsor and security-agency consultation for mission issuance; the Afghanistan-mission route says it may allow ordinary nationals a multiple-entry visa. Those discretionary, security and route conditions cannot be represented as one ordinary-passport short-visitor status.
